draft.title: How one economy affects another
card: Countries trade by selling exports to other countries and buying imports from them. One country's imports are another country's exports.
When an economy slows, people earn less or worry about their jobs. They spend less, including on imported goods.
Countries that export to the slowing economy then sell less to it. Their exporting businesses lose sales.
With fewer sales, those businesses may cut production and jobs. In this way a slowdown in one economy can spread to others.
draft.remember: A slowing economy buys fewer imports, so its trading partners lose export sales and jobs.

a.q: A country's economy slows and its people buy fewer imports. What is the effect on countries that export to it?
opts: They sell less, so their exporters may lose sales and jobs
They sell more, as the slowing country needs cheaper goods
They are unaffected, as only the slowing country is hurt
They must stop trading with that country
a.why: One country's imports are its partners' exports, so fewer imports means fewer export sales for them. The effect is not nothing, since the exporters depend on that buyer.
a.clue: One country's imports are another country's exports.

b.q: Farmers in Tasmania export much of their fruit to Country X. Country X's economy slows sharply. What is the most likely effect on the farmers?
opts: Fewer sales to Country X, so they may cut output and jobs
More sales to Country X, as buyers look for cheaper food
No effect, because fruit is a necessity for all buyers
Higher wages, as demand from Country X rises
b.why: Households in Country X earn less and buy fewer imports, so exports of fruit to it may fall and farmers may cut jobs. Fruit being food does not guarantee the sales, as the card says a slowdown reduces spending on imports.
b.clue: Who is buying less when their own economy slows?

a.best: They sell less, so their exporters may lose sales and jobs

b.best: Fewer sales to Country X, so they may cut output and jobs

proposal.title: How one economy affects another
card: Countries trade by selling exports to other countries and buying imports from them. One country's imports are another country's exports.
When an economy slows, people earn less or worry about their jobs. They spend less, including on imported goods.
Countries that export to the slowing economy then sell less to it. Their exporting businesses lose sales.
With fewer sales, those businesses may cut production and jobs. In this way a slowdown in one economy can spread to others.
proposal.remember: A slowing economy tends to buy fewer imports, which can cost its trading partners sales and jobs.

a.q: Country Z's economy slows and many of its households earn less. What tends to happen to businesses in other countries that export to Z?
opts: Sales to Z tend to fall, as Z's people spend less
Sales to Z tend to rise, as Z's people want cheaper goods
Sales to Z stay the same, as a slowdown stays inside Z
Sales to Z tend to rise, as Z now makes fewer goods itself
a.why: When people in Z earn less, they spend less, including on imports. Z's imports are other countries' exports, so those exporters sell less to Z. A slowdown does not stay inside Z, because its spending is income for businesses elsewhere.
a.clue: Think about what people do with their spending when they earn less.

b.q: Farmers in Tasmania export much of their fruit to Country X. Country X's economy slows sharply. What is the most likely effect on the farmers?
opts: Fewer sales to Country X, so they may cut output and jobs
More sales to Country X, so they may take on more workers
Steady sales to Country X, so they may keep all their jobs
Fewer sales to Country X, so they may hire more workers
b.why: People in Country X earn less and spend less, including on imported fruit, so the farmers sell less and may cut output and jobs. Steady sales is tempting because fruit is food, but a slowdown cuts spending on imports, so the farmers' sales to Country X are still likely to fall.
b.clue: Who is spending less when their own economy slows?

a.best: Sales to Z tend to fall, as Z's people spend less

b.best: Fewer sales to Country X, so they may cut output and jobs
